title: IV. Abrogation; Cap.10 next on the Gospel
pass_a_gloss: Pass A clause gloss (reordered): CHAPTER TEN follows, On ye Gospel: where also on ye Apostles' Creed. — Simple observation stands as neither forbidden nor absolutely prescribed toward any people, except what rests on common right and natural equity. What as toward substance and chief end looks toward Christ, no people may usurp. Refer Josephus, Philo, Maimonides, Sigonius, Bertram, and Cunaeus On ye Jewish Commonwealth. — IV. Abrogation does not remove ye common equity founded in nature's light; yet insofar as ye law looked toward Christ, it stands as abrogated universally.
pass_b_english: IV. Abrogation does not remove the common equity founded in nature's light; yet insofar as the law looked to Christ, it is abrogated universally.

Simple observation is neither forbidden nor absolutely prescribed to any people, except what rests on common right and natural equity. What as to substance and chief end looks to Christ, no people may usurp. Refer Josephus, Philo, Maimonides, Sigonius, Bertram, and Cunaeus On the Jewish Commonwealth.
CHAPTER TEN follows, On the Gospel: where also on the Apostles' Creed.
source_text: IV. Abrogatio legis forensis non quidem tollit communem aequitatem in ipso naturae lumine fundatam; quatenus tamen Christum respexit, abrogata est haec lex universe. Quantum ad simplicem observationem, neque prohibita est neque praescripta ulli populo absoluta necessitate, si excipiantur quae communis iuris sunt & naturali aequitate nituntur. Quae vero quoad substantiam & finem praecipuum in Christum respiciunt, nulli populo licet usurpare. Huc refer Josephum, Philonem, Maimonidem, Sigonium, Bertramum, & Petrum Cunaeum de republica Judaeorum. CAPUT DECIMUM sequitur, De Euangelio: ubi de Symbolo Apostolorum.
